questions.question: Where should students wait for a school bus?

options.text: At the designated bus stop.
Anywhere, and the driver will pick them up.
Wherever their parents choose.

questions.explanation: A school bus driver can only pick up and drop off students at bus stops approved by the school district.

questions.question: What is true about students loading and unloading a bus?

options.text: It is safe and does not need supervision.
It can be dangerous and must be supervised.
It can happen without the driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous and must be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. A bus driver must always supervise this process.

questions.question: If a bus must be evacuated, where is safest for students to go?

options.text: Within 50 feet of the bus.
Downwind if there is a fire.
Far away from railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: After leaving the bus, students should go at least 100 feet away from the road toward oncoming traffic. They should be upwind of any fire and as far from railroad tracks as possible.

questions.question: What should you NOT do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass a slow vehicle on the tracks.
Get out to check for a train.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: On the right side of the bus.
On the steering wheel.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive in high winds?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: A school bus can be pushed by wind because of its large sides. In windy conditions, grip the wheel firmly, watch for wind gusts, and slow down.

questions.question: What should you do if a student has a back injury?

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Do not move them.
Tell them to try standing up.

questions.explanation: Do not move a student with a neck or spine injury unless their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted flat mirrors on a school bus show?

options.text: The sides of the bus.
The ground under the bus.
The front tires touching the ground.

questions.explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors show 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.

questions.question: What must happen if there is a fire on a school bus?

options.text: Students must leave the bus.
Students should stay on but move away from the fire.
Students should stay in their seats.

questions.explanation: If a bus is on fire or might catch fire, the driver must immediately evacuate all students.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on driving maneuvers and general behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly, obey all traffic rules, and avoid accidents and violations.

questions.question: How should you do a basic parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it slowly. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Lock up your wheels.
Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: Watch the students on the bus.
Look at the outside of the bus.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the inside rearview mirror helps you watch all the students. Adjust it so you can see every student, including those right behind you.

questions.question: Where should students sit when boarding a bus?

options.text: In the back row first.
In the back row only after all other seats are filled.
As far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting closer to the front is safer in case the bus is hit from behind. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: During a vehicle control test, what is a look?

options.text: Checking the gauges on your dashboard.
Checking your blind spots.
Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out of your seat and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look is when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of your vehicle to check where it is. During straight line backing, you can only do one look. During other exercises, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: How should a driver approach a bus stop?

options.text: Without using the mirrors.
Slowly and carefully.
Quickly and stop suddenly.

questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and with care.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted on a school bus?

options.text: While driving.
Before you start driving.
By the students.

questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving a school bus.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not try to drive around the gate.

questions.question: If a tornado is near and there is no shelter, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch
To the closest tree
Near a river

questions.explanation: If a tornado is coming and there is no building, take students to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood. Stay far enough away so the bus cannot fall on them if it tips over.

questions.question: Before opening the bus door to pick up students, what must happen?

options.text: All surrounding traffic must stop.
Turn on the alternating red lights.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Before you open the door and tell students to board, make sure all traffic around the bus has stopped.
